GearShed — the clickable version

Design step 7, built 28/09/2026 from the approved wireframes (gearshed-wireframes.mockup.html) and lofi/links.json by lofi/build.py. Grey on purpose: this tests whether the paths work, not how the app looks.

Start tappingPick New rider or Wouter

Open it on your phone

  1. In Terminal on the Mac: cd ~/Claude/Projects/Personal/bike-maintenance/nimbalyst-local/mockups && python3 -m http.server 8000. If the Mac asks whether Python may accept incoming connections, click Allow.
  2. In a second Terminal window: ipconfig getifaddr en0 || ipconfig getifaddr en1. It prints the Mac's address, like 192.168.1.20.
  3. On the phone, on the same Wi-Fi, open http://192.168.1.20:8000/gearshed-lofi.mockup.html with the Mac's address.
  4. When you are done, press Control-C in the first Terminal window. Nothing is put online.

How it works

  • Tap something linked and the next screen opens. Tap anything else and every linked spot on the screen flashes blue for 0.6 s: it shows what can be tapped, and where a path stops.
  • Start again, under the phone, goes back to the two ways in. The browser's back button works, and every screen has its own address.
  • Not simulated: typing, ticking, switches, scrolling and swipes. The values drawn on each screen stand. A long screen shows its top part only. To close a sheet, tap its Cancel, ‹, Undo or Done: swiping it down does nothing here.
  • An open menu closes on any tap outside it, as on an iPhone: the tap does nothing else.
  • Numbers can disagree between screens. The screens were drawn at different moments of Wouter's month, so a job you just logged can still show as due on the next screen. The paths are tested here, not the data.
  • Undecided parts are hidden: the dashed boxes of the wireframes. A rider sees only what is decided.

The 14 main paths

The 13 first-version jobs of 09-structure.md §3, plus the first run. Give your shop access is v1, so it is left out. Counted from where each rider starts: New rider on Welcome, Wouter on Due, where the app opens. Taps to its screen stops where §3's count stops; §3 counted from a Garage landing, before the app opened on Due. Taps to done adds the taps that finish the job. Counts that differ are not forced to match: the difference goes to the tap recount (BIM.62).

Who this design assumes the rider is

Wouter Claes, who fixes his own bikes (02-personas.md §1; the person is fiction built from the rider corpus, his needs are KNOWN from it). Four bikes: a trail mountain bike, a hardtail, a gravel bike with two wheelsets, a road bike. Two to three waxed chains per bike, swapped in rotation (reddit[2]#c39, reddit[2]#c45). He does every job himself except the fork and damper rebuild, which goes to his shop. His kilometres are in Strava or Garmin Connect today. The screens assume his words: chain, cassette, sealant, wax, rotor, chain checker. The New rider path assumes the same kind of rider: a gravel bike, a waxed rotation of three chains.

Does it push the rider, and who does it leave out?

The deceptive-pattern check: no fake urgency, no hidden cost, nothing harder to cancel than to start. The bias check: who the screens quietly assume, and who they shut out. One line per group of screens.

ScreensDoes it push the rider?Who it assumes, who it leaves out
Welcome, sign in (11)No timer, nothing ticked for you. No account is asked for before the first bike. The account offer names its reason (a new phone would lose the garage) and can be ignored. Deleting an account takes 4 taps (Settings, Your account, Delete everything, confirm): the confirmation is there because it cannot be undone, and Export everything first sits on it. It is not hidden: it is on Your account, next to Sign outNobody needs an account to start (your call 1, B). Leaves out: a rider who never makes one loses the garage with the phone; export is the safety net. To sign up, it assumes an Apple or Google account or an email address
Due (1, 10)No fake urgency: every ■ ▲ ◇ has its real number beside it, counted from rides. No badges, nothing to buyAssumes kilometres; miles live in Language · help · about, not drawn yet. Shapes and numbers, not colour alone, so a colour-blind rider reads it
Garage: bike, part, swap, shelf, add a part (2–6, 16)Every swap, wax and add ends in Undo and Done, no timer. Retire is neutral; Delete is red and asks first. The swap picks To the shelf for you, which keeps the chainAssumes a waxed rotation and the gravel bike drawing. An oiled chain gets Log lube and a belt its own kit (sections 3, 8). Leaves out bike types with no drawing yet (cargo, tandem, recumbent) until step 12
Add a bike (7, 8)Every kit part has its own switch, seen before saving. Skip is at the topFive bike types. The family's cargo bike and the children's bikes that share Wouter's garage are not offered (02-personas.md §1, Family)
Log a session, log a service (10, 15)Save says what it resets before you press it. Cost, notes and photos are optionalAssumes he does the work or names My shop. A rider whose shop does everything has little to log until shops can write entries (A1)
Part settings, Measure (13, 14)Nothing sits behind a plan. Cancel or ‹ on every stepAssumes a chain checker from the listed makers; a caliper and a digital tool are there. A rider with no tool gets the estimate only
History, export (17, 18)Export is free, always (PRD.md §10): one file, no format to get wrong. Nothing locks the record inCSV and JSON assume a spreadsheet or another app. A buyer who wants a PDF waits for v1
Rides (19, 20)A ride is held, never guessed onto a bike. Moving a ride shows what it changed, with UndoAssumes Strava or typing by hand. A rider with only a Garmin types by hand at launch: Garmin's programme is closed to new apps (BIM.12)
Settings: sources, notifications, account (12, 21, 22)Connecting and disconnecting Strava are both 3 taps. Notifications start at one per due part, push only, email off (your call 2); one digest a day and Off are one tap away on the same screen. Your plan is not drawn: check it for hidden cost when billing is drawn (M6)English only. Units sit in a screen not drawn yet

Checked against earlier decisions

Decision or inputWhere the clickable version follows it
The app opens on Due (BIM.38, 25/09/2026)Wouter starts on Due. Moving a wheelset from Due takes 4 taps, the cost BIM.38 accepted: path 10
Four tabs, Due · Garage · Rides · Settings (BIM.41, 28/09/2026)tabs in links.json: every tab bar goes to the same four screens. Under a sheet's shade the tabs do nothing
No account before the first bike (your call 1, BIM.69, changed from A to B on 28/09/2026 to follow Apple: "Delay sign-in as long as possible")New rider starts on Welcome, version B. The account is offered once after the first bike and in Settings, behind one door: Continue with Apple, Google or email. Version A's Welcome is not in this file. PRD.md §5.1 still says account first until the write-back (BIM.62)
Only the versions you picked (BIM.58, BIM.63, BIM.69)links.json names only picked phones, and the build copies only the phones it names
A sheet never opens another sheet (Apple HIG, sheets)A sheet's links go to its own next step, or close it. The share sheet opens after the export sheet closes
Every save confirms with Undo and Done, no timer (BIM.60 comment, 26/09/2026)Every path that saves ends on that sheet, except two. The first run ends on the Garage's own one-time line about the shelf (close-up A4, approved before this rule). Part settings' Done applies at once, like the phone's own Settings, so path 12 ends on the chain page. Undo and Done go back to the screen the sheet was drawn over. Five sheets were missing and are drawn now; Measure's changes a section 3 note
Notifications: when a part is due, push on, email off (your call 2, BIM.69)Section 22 now shows it; path 8 picks the digest
A wheel area opens its sheet, Swap wheelset first (section 2's tap rule)Drawn as a new phone in section 2, for path 10
Status is a shape and a number, not colour alone (08-flows.md §4)Unchanged. The blue flash is the only colour, and it only marks what can be tapped
Tap counts: the real count next to the sitemap's, never forced (spec §5)The paths table above; the differences are a comment on BIM.62
